Both probes must sample the same granulate volume at the same time or be synchronized to a common time step, and each method needs its own calibration. The fused model must beat the best single-method NIR model on held-out batches; otherwise the extra Raman instrument is not justified.)

items.finding: The review notes that temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solutions by NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This supports measuring or controlling temperature at the NIR measurement point, since temperature variation could affect the moisture-related signal. It could inform whether the proposed setup needs a temperature sensor or tempered sampling interface.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement concerns aqueous solutions in NIR/MIR and tempered sample holders, not granulate moisture or an in-line granulate probe. Transfer to the customer's matrix and measurement geometry would need testing.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: The review states that before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate each dataset's contribution to the model and its complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: This supports a staged data-fusion assessment: first check whether Raman adds complementary information to NIR, then compare the fused model against the best single-method NIR model on held-out batches. It could inform what to test before justifying the extra Raman instrument.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is general guidance from a PAT data-fusion review, not a result for NIR/Raman fusion of granulate moisture. The specific sample, probe volumes, synchronization, and calibration approach would still need experimental verification.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E02 ¶82

items.finding: The review reports that in some situations instrument complementarity alone was not sufficient to improve prediction of several CQAs in a Raman and FT-IR food analytical study.
items.how_it_applies: This is a caution that adding a second spectroscopy method may not improve the model even if the instruments seem complementary. It supports requiring the fused NIR/Raman model to outperform the best single-method NIR model before accepting the extended option.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited case is a Raman and FT-IR food analytical study, not NIR and Raman on granulate moisture. Its outcome may not transfer to different samples, matrices, instruments, or fusion methods.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E02 ¶36
